findings.ref: staged resolver Python master (human-copy candidate), _atomic_write_bytes directory-fsync comment, lines 1521-1526; vs verification/T-007/mutation-proofs.log MUTANT M; vs implementation report Rounds 33-35 entry
findings.note: The report's Rounds 33-35 entry states: 'The stale in-process-unobservability comment mutant M's kill had disproved is corrected in place.' It is not corrected in the shipped bytes. The only unobservability comment in the resolver, at mutant M's own anchor site in _atomic_write_bytes, still reads 'Not observable by any in-process fixture ... so this hardening is disclosed as uncovered in the mutation log rather than implied to be tested', while the declared mutation log at the same declared sha256 (c26c968c...) kills mutant M at 395 passed / 3 failed and its own note says COVERED, the CALL being observable via the fault-injection overlay. This is a live contradiction between two declared outputs about what the evidence covers, and the current round entry affirmatively claims a remediation that is absent from the artifact it declares. The resolver bytes in the bundle postdate round 35 (they carry the round-35 staging-chain comment and the removed explicit fsync pair), so this is not a stale-copy artifact of bundling. Behavior is unaffected and the coverage error runs in the conservative direction, but a false corrected-in-place claim in the newest verification narrative is the amendment-propagation class this package has repeatedly had graded Major, and it means the round-35 self-description was not re-verified against the shipped bytes.
